scenes.title: A shop and a quiet shopper
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Imagine running a furniture shop with products ready to sell, while a shopper who could buy from you has gone quiet.

scenes.title: A reason to reach out
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: In our simulated market, this shopper hasn't bought for sixteen days. Sending everyone a discount is easy, but finding a recommendation worth sending takes evidence.

scenes.title: Connect the evidence
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: So Market Metro first connects the shopper, product and payment records. Its ontology keeps split merchant orders tied to one checkout, and holds any links it can't trust.

scenes.title: Build the campaign
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: With that evidence, the agent examines demand and stock, chooses twenty eight days of training data, and asks local tools to fit two models for a reactivation campaign.
onScreen: 28-day history → LLM agent → 2 model fits → campaign

scenes.title: Test before sending
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: The first idea doesn't get a free pass. A verifier tests both rankings in separate development markets and selects the one that earns more while protecting merchants.

scenes.title: The recommendation becomes a purchase
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: On day thirty five, the selected recommendation reaches our shopper. They buy a ninety six dollar side table, and it arrives the next day; fixed rules left that same request unfilled.

scenes.title: A payment you can trace
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: We mirror that order once through PayPal Sandbox. The completed capture records the fee and merchant proceeds, then returns a receipt that links all the way back to the purchase.

scenes.title: What changed
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Across this twelve store simulation, the campaign delivers sixteen extra retained purchases, over a thousand dollars in merchant contribution, and three point four seven percent more modeled PayPal net.

scenes.title: Follow the full trail
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Judges can follow the whole trail in AG Grid, from model training and the agent's decision to the PayPal receipt, instead of taking the result on trust.

uploadDraft.title: Market Metro | Agentic Commerce That Learns | PayPal AI Hackathon
uploadDraft.description:
Market Metro turns observed merchant activity into trained models, tested campaigns and traceable PayPal payments. This demo follows one saved 12-store, 600-shopper simulation from Day 1 to a recorded agent decision, purchase and native PayPal Sandbox receipt.

Against fixed rules in that same simulation: 16 more retained purchases, $1,024.86 additional merchant contribution, and $114.96 higher modeled PayPal net after estimated model cost. Merchant contribution includes inventory value. These are simulated outcomes, not actual PayPal profit. The $96 Sandbox capture is an existing order and uses fictitious funds.

Built with PayPal Sandbox, Gemini on Vertex AI, local scikit-learn models, SQLite, Three.js and AG Studio with native AG Grid, AG Charts and a custom PayPal evidence widget. The ontology feed comparison is a separate synthetic-data test.

Source and setup: https://github.com/VinceVence/market-metro
Original code: MIT. Third-party components retain their own licenses.
